terms.definition: A type that groups related values together, and every copy you make is independent of the others.
terms.example: I made the user profile a struct, so changing a copy does not touch the original.

terms.definition: A type that groups data and actions together, and it can inherit from a parent type.
terms.example: The view controller is a class, because UIKit needs it to inherit from UIViewController.

terms.definition: A type where many variables point to the same single instance, so a change through one variable shows up in all of them.
terms.example: Because it is a reference type, both screens see the update as soon as one of them changes it.

quizzes.question: Which one is a type that can inherit from a parent type?
Which one means many variables share one instance, so a change shows up everywhere?
Which one is a type that groups related values, where every copy is independent?

Today's terms
Struct - A type that groups related values together, and every copy you make is independent of the others.
Class - A type that groups data and actions together, and it can inherit from a parent type.
Reference Type - A type where many variables point to the same single instance, so a change through one variable shows up in all of them.
